facts.desired_state: The production workflow deploys through the same core the CLI uses, holds only a scoped token, serialises deployments, and its token is installed without ever appearing in a log or a file.
non_scope: An account-wide token in CI
A CI-only container build implementation separate from the canonical one
Weakening the token model because a tool was unavailable
facts.risk: Cancelling an in-progress deployment can leave a machine half-updated. Whether cancellation is safe is a decision to make explicitly, not a default to inherit.

nodes.label: I0930
nodes.summary: The real image runs under the real limits before anything is deployed

acceptance_criteria: The image under test is the production image, built by the canonical build
It runs under the declared memory and CPU limits of the cheap profile, and with a read-only filesystem where the application permits it
The process stays alive, its user id is not zero, and it listens on the declared port
Liveness and readiness answer, and the landing, documentation, API document and static assets are served
Readiness is reached by bounded polling on an ephemeral port, with no sleep and no fixed port
facts.current_state: No image and no container test exist.
facts.desired_state: One test builds the production image, runs it constrained, polls readiness with a bounded timeout, and asserts the behaviour the deployment depends on.
non_scope: A fixed host port
A sleep standing in for readiness
A test image that differs from the production one
facts.objective: Build the actual production image and run it under the resource limits of the cheap profile, verifying the process, its user, its port and its routes without fixed ports and without sleeping.
facts.risk: A container test needs a container runtime, which not every environment has. It must skip explicitly and visibly where the runtime is absent rather than passing quietly.

nodes.label: I0931
nodes.summary: The application exists, one machine runs it, and the URL answers

facts.current_state: No application exists at any provider.
facts.desired_state: One application, one machine, the declared resources, the declared region, a public HTTPS URL that answers, a smoke suite that passes against it, and a machine-readable report of what was deployed.
non_scope: Creating a new application on any subsequent deploy
Mutating or deleting any unrelated application
Accepting a deploy command's exit code as verification
facts.risk: This is the issue that spends money and touches a real account. It runs once the container evidence is in, and the inventory assertion is what keeps a mistake from billing indefinitely.
facts.why: Everything before this is preparation. A deployment that has never run is a hypothesis, and an exit code from a deploy command is not evidence that anything is being served.

nodes.label: I0932
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The measured baselines — binary, image, context, build durations, readiness, resident memory, endpoint latency — are documented with the machine and environment they were measured on
The developer workflow in the documentation runs exactly as written on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: The milestone is accepted with evidence against every criterion, and the baselines and limitations are written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a plan as an implementation
Recording a measurement without the environment it was taken on
facts.risk: The temptation at the end is to record intent as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is a limitation, and it is written as one.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. The numbers, the commands and the deployed URL are what a later reader has; this session's messages are not.

nodes.label: I1001
nodes.summary: One typed graph composes the registries that already own their facts

acceptance_criteria: Node kinds come from the kinds the layer already registers, and adding a kind does not require a new variant hand-written in the graph
Every source is read through the registry that owns it, never by a second traversal of the filesystem
Generation over identical repository contents produces structurally identical output, with no iteration-order dependence, no random identity and no timestamp inside the canonical data
The model separates a capability's definition from its runtime state, so that the static projection needs no runtime fields
Unit tests cover discovery, normalisation, deduplication and ordering
facts.current_state: graph.rs derives rule dependencies, decisions and the shape of the layer for the Cockpit and the site. The capability registry knows capabilities. Nothing joins the two, and no node type spans both.
facts.desired_state: One typed model holds nodes of every kind the repository already indexes, built by reading the registries through the paths every other caller uses, and producing the same output for the same inputs.
non_scope: A new store of anything an existing registry already owns
Reading the index outside the executor, the cache and the counters that every other read passes through
Node kinds invented here rather than taken from the kinds the layer already registers
facts.risk: Composing everything invites a model that knows too much and is slower than the hot path allows. It is built on the reads that already happen, and its cost is measured like every other command's.

nodes.label: I1002
nodes.summary: Relations are typed, inferred from stable identities, and never dangle

acceptance_criteria: Each relation type is explicit, and the direction is part of its meaning
Inference uses stable identities only, and an ambiguous case requires an explicit declaration instead of a guess
A relation whose target does not exist fails generation, naming where it was declared and what is missing
Tests cover malformed metadata, duplicate identities and dangling relations
facts.current_state: Relations exist implicitly in frontmatter references, capability tags, rule metadata and ADR related lists. Nothing resolves them into a common edge type, and nothing fails when one does not resolve.
facts.desired_state: Every edge has a type, both ends resolve to a node, and an unresolvable edge fails generation with a message naming the declaration, the missing end and the correction.
non_scope: Inference by substring or title matching where a stable identity exists
Requiring a contributor to restate a relation the metadata already implies
facts.risk: Strict resolution can make an unrelated documentation edit fail the build. The message has to be good enough that the failure is a five-second fix rather than an investigation.

nodes.label: I1003
nodes.summary: Skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases and benchmarks enter the graph as themselves

acceptance_criteria: Each kind is projected from its own registry with the metadata that registry holds, and no field is invented here
A rule shows what it governs, how it is enforced and what tests it; a skill shows its purpose, scope and relations; a decision shows what it puts in force
Adding a valid object under a canonical directory makes it appear in the graph with no further registration
Where a relation needs declaring, the field is added to the kind's existing schema rather than to a new one
facts.current_state: Each kind is indexed and readable as an object. The site renders some of them as lists. None is related to a capability by anything a machine reads.
facts.desired_state: Each kind is a node with the metadata its own registry holds, related to what it governs, documents, enforces, tests or measures.
non_scope: A second registry for any of these kinds
Frontmatter conventions that conflict with the schemas those directories already define
facts.risk: Every kind has its own vocabulary, and flattening them into one node type loses what makes each useful. The node carries the kind's own metadata rather than a lowest common denominator.

nodes.label: I1004
nodes.summary: Availability and visibility are metadata, not conditions in a template

acceptance_criteria: Availability distinguishes at least what is always true, what requires the running backend, what is a build-time snapshot and what requires authentication
Visibility distinguishes public and developer-facing capabilities from ones deliberately marked internal
Every existing capability, route and surface is classified, and an unclassified one is a validation failure rather than a default
No projection decides availability from anything other than this metadata
facts.current_state: The Cockpit is served by the running process. The site is generated. Nothing states which capability means anything in which environment.
facts.desired_state: Availability and visibility are fields of the model, every projection reads them, and no template decides for itself.
non_scope: Any decision made from a hostname, a URL or a build-time flag inside a template
An internal capability being silently invisible without saying it is internal
facts.risk: A default of always-available makes the model useless and the classification invisible. Absence has to be a failure.

nodes.label: I1005
nodes.summary: The graph is a generated artifact with a schema and no unsafe field

acceptance_criteria: The artifact is produced by the existing generation target set, not by a separate script
It has a schema, and the schema is generated from the types rather than written by hand
Ordering is deterministic and repeated generation is byte-identical over identical inputs
It contains no credential, no private environment value and no machine-absolute path, proved by a test
Provenance is recorded in the artifact's own metadata where its format cannot carry a comment
facts.current_state: No aggregate artifact exists. The site reads several derived datasets, each from its own script.
facts.desired_state: One generated artifact carries the graph, with a schema, deterministic ordering, provenance and no field that must not be published.
non_scope: A hand-edited copy of the artifact
Any token, key, header, environment dump or machine-absolute path in the output
A timestamp inside the canonical data
facts.objective: Serialise the graph as a deterministic generated artifact with a schema, carrying safe metadata only, produced by the generation the repository already runs.
facts.risk: One artifact for everything grows until it is downloaded on every page load. Its size is measured and budgeted with the other assets.
facts.why: Both projections and every test need one file to read. Making it generated keeps it honest; giving it a schema makes it consumable; keeping it free of anything private makes it publishable.

nodes.label: I1006
nodes.summary: The runtime reads the graph through the registry, like every other read

acceptance_criteria: The operation is one capability declaration and appears in the API, the OpenAPI document, the reference and the benchmark coverage without a second registration
The response is typed and carries safe fields only
Runtime state is an overlay over the definitions, distinguishable in the response
A test exercises the operation against a running server rather than a mock
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders in-process. No capability serves the aggregate graph.
facts.desired_state: One declared capability serves the graph, documented and benchmarked like the rest, with the runtime state layered over the definitions rather than mixed into them.
non_scope: A route registered outside the capability registry
Runtime state stored in the same structure as the definitions
facts.objective: Expose the graph to the running Cockpit as a declared capability, so that its route, its schema, its documentation and its benchmark coverage all follow from the declaration.
facts.risk: Serving the whole graph on every Cockpit load is a cost on the hot path. It is measured, and paged or filtered if the measurement says so.
facts.why: A route added by hand for the Cockpit would be the one endpoint missing from OpenAPI, from the reference and from the smoke suite. The registry exists precisely so that does not happen.

nodes.label: I1007
nodes.summary: The site renders the same graph, generated once

acceptance_criteria: The static projection is produced by the canonical generation target set, with any shell involved being a thin adapter
The published pages render the capabilities, the kinds, the relations and the coverage without any request to a backend
Build-time and runtime data are distinguishable on the page, and a captured measurement is labelled as captured rather than shown as current
The drift check covers the static projection
facts.current_state: The site is generated from the registry and several derived datasets by scripts that each know their own output.
facts.desired_state: The static projection is a target of the canonical generation, and the site consumes it like its other derived data.
non_scope: A standalone cockpit generation script
The static build requiring any runtime API to render
facts.risk: Rendering yesterday's health as though it were current is the failure mode this issue exists to prevent, and it is a labelling problem, not a data problem.
facts.why: A separate generation script for the site is the second universe this repository has already refused once. The generation target set exists and owns this.

nodes.label: I1008
nodes.summary: The two projections are proved to be the same model

acceptance_criteria: The comparison is over the normalised model, not over HTML
Runtime-only fields are removed by an explicit list that the test owns, so adding one to either side without declaring it fails
The test runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: Only one projection exists today, so there is nothing to compare.
facts.desired_state: One test builds both, strips the runtime-only fields and asserts equality, and it fails when either projection grows a field the other does not know about.
non_scope: Asserting equality of rendered markup rather than of the model
facts.objective: Test that the static and runtime representations of the graph are equal once runtime-only fields are removed, so the published site and the running server cannot become alternate realities.
facts.risk: A parity test that strips too much passes trivially. The stripped list is small, explicit and reviewed.
facts.why: Two renderings of one model diverge silently, and the divergence is discovered by a person who trusted the wrong one. A parity test is the only thing that keeps them honest.

nodes.label: I1009
nodes.summary: Every menu in this repository comes from one derivation

acceptance_criteria: Every navigation surface reads the same projection, and none holds its own list
Grouping derives from metadata the model already carries, and ordering is deterministic and stable across builds
Adding a capability or a document changes every menu that should show it with no template edit
An entry unavailable in the current environment is not rendered as an active destination
facts.current_state: Navigation and landing content are assembled per surface. The landing page and the Cockpit each know their own entries.
facts.desired_state: One navigation projection feeds every surface, grouping derives from kind, category, scope and availability, and ordering is deterministic.
non_scope: Any hand-written menu entry in a template, a script or a data file
Layout coordinates, columns or component trees expressed as data
facts.why: Five menus mean five edits for one new page, and the fifth is the one everybody forgets. Grouping by facts the model already holds gives an order that is stable without anyone maintaining it.

nodes.label: I1010
nodes.summary: The overview is what exists, counted rather than claimed

acceptance_criteria: Sections are present only when the corresponding kind has members
Every number shown is computed from the graph at build or request time
A kind added to the layer appears in the overview with no change to the overview's own code
The counts on the page match the artifact, proved by a test
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders pages derived from the registry and the index. Section presence and any counts are decided in code.
facts.desired_state: Sections appear because their kind has members, counts are computed, and a new kind of thing appears without the overview being rewritten.
non_scope: A number typed by a human anywhere in the interface
A heading rendered for a kind with no members
facts.objective: Generate the Cockpit overview and its summary numbers from the graph, showing a section only when the repository actually holds that kind of thing.
facts.risk: Counts on a page are the sort of thing the repository's own rule against numbers in prose exists for. They are computed and rendered, never written.
facts.why: A dashboard with headings for things that do not exist teaches readers to distrust it, and hand-maintained counts are wrong within a week. Both problems disappear when the overview is a query.

nodes.label: I1011
nodes.summary: The coverage matrix reports evidence, and never a green cell without one

acceptance_criteria: Every filled cell names the artifact that supports it and can be followed to it
A relation that claims evidence but does not resolve is reported as a gap, and the report says which end failed
The policy for what evidence a kind requires is data, not a condition in the renderer, and a descriptive kind is not asked for a behavioural test
The matrix is available in both projections and in machine-readable form
facts.current_state: Benchmark coverage exists for capabilities. Documentation, tests and enforcement have no coverage view at all.
facts.desired_state: Each cell resolves to a named artifact — a document, a test, a rule, a benchmark case — and an unresolved claim is reported as missing rather than shown as satisfied.
non_scope: A status a contributor can declare without an artifact behind it
Demanding evidence from purely descriptive metadata that has no behaviour to test
facts.objective: Generate a matrix showing, for every capability, whether it is documented, tested, enforced, benchmarked and exposed, where each cell resolves to an artifact or a relation rather than to a claim.
facts.risk: A matrix that is mostly empty on the first run will be read as an indictment rather than a baseline. It is a starting measurement, and saying so is part of shipping it.

nodes.label: I1012
nodes.summary: One detail view, assembled from what a node actually has

acceptance_criteria: Empty sections are absent rather than rendered blank
The deep link is built from the stable identity and survives a title change
Source references are repository-relative and never machine-absolute
The static projection produces compatible links
facts.current_state: The Cockpit renders views over the registry. Deep links and source traceability are not part of the model.
facts.desired_state: One assembly renders any node, showing only populated sections, with a stable link and a repository-relative source reference.
non_scope: A separate hardcoded template per kind unless the presentation genuinely differs
A machine-absolute path in any published output
Identity derived from a display title
facts.objective: Render a capability's detail page from its populated sections and its resolved relations, with a stable deep link and a repository-relative reference to where the information came from.
facts.risk: Traceability that publishes a path from the machine that built the site is a leak. Repository-relative is the only form that ships.

nodes.label: I1013
nodes.summary: Search over the graph, generated, with nothing to run

acceptance_criteria: The index is generated from the graph and covers identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents
Search works in the static build with no backend
A newly registered capability is findable after generation with no further edit
The index size is measured and counted against the asset budget
facts.current_state: No unified search exists over the layer.
facts.desired_state: One generated index serves both projections, its contents derive from the graph, and it costs nothing to operate.
non_scope: An external search service for a graph of this size
A hand-maintained index or keyword list
facts.objective: Provide one search over identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents, from a generated index that works in the static build with no service behind it.
facts.risk: A client-side index grows with the repository until it dominates the page weight. Measuring it now is what makes the later decision to page or trim it a measurement rather than a surprise.
facts.why: A repository this size does not need a search service, and adding one would put the published site behind an availability dependency it currently does not have.

nodes.label: I1014
nodes.summary: The relation view reads the graph and holds no data of its own

acceptance_criteria: Every node and edge comes from the generated data
Filters operate on the model's fields — kind, category, source, surface, availability, relation type and the evidence flags
Zoom, pan, selection, neighbour highlighting, a detail panel and deep links all work, and a selected node resolves to its detail view
The library is lazily loaded and absent from pages without a graph
A textual equivalent of the same relations is available for anyone who cannot use the graph
Initialisation cost on this repository's data is measured
facts.current_state: The layer's graphs are derived and rendered for the site. There is no interactive relation view over the composed model.
facts.desired_state: One view reads the artifact, filters by the model's own fields, and is not loaded by pages that do not use it.
non_scope: Nodes or edges written into JavaScript
A visualisation library loaded on pages that do not render a graph
A three-dimensional rendering that replaces rather than supplements the accessible information
facts.objective: Render the relation graph interactively from the generated data, with filters, focus, neighbour highlighting and deep links, loaded only where it is used and bounded in cost.
facts.risk: Rendering every node at once is slow and unreadable at the same time. The default view is filtered, and expansion is progressive.
facts.why: The edges are the reason the model exists, and a static list cannot show them. But a visualisation with nodes written into a script is a second inventory in the least maintainable place available.

nodes.label: I1015
nodes.summary: A surface with no server behind it is not offered as if it had one

acceptance_criteria: A backend-only surface is offered as usable only where a backend is available, decided from metadata
The static build contains no active link to a runtime-only surface
Where mentioning an unavailable surface is useful, it is shown as unavailable rather than omitted silently or linked
Both cases are tested — the static build and a running server with the API present
facts.current_state: The Swagger shell and the API are served by the running process. The published site has no way to know that.
facts.desired_state: Exposure follows from availability metadata alone, and there is a test for each projection that keeps it that way.
non_scope: Any decision made from a hostname, an address or a build flag inside a page
Rendering a dead destination as if it were live
facts.objective: Make the exposure of backend-only surfaces — the API console, live status, runtime reads — follow from availability metadata, and prove both projections behave correctly.
facts.risk: This is the check that quietly rots, because a broken link on a published page fails nothing. The test for it has to run on every build.
facts.why: The published site has no server. A link to a runtime console on it is a broken promise, and the usual fix is a check on the page's own address, which is a rule hidden where nobody will find it.

nodes.label: I1016
nodes.summary: The Cockpit works on a phone and before JavaScript runs

acceptance_criteria: Navigation, content, tables and details are usable at narrow phone widths through to a wide desktop, with no horizontal page overflow at any of them
Touch targets are usable and focus is visible
The markup is semantic, keyboard navigation works, and status is never conveyed by colour alone
Core information is present in the served HTML before enhancement
facts.current_state: The Cockpit is server-rendered with its own stylesheet, and its behaviour across viewports has not been established for this material.
facts.desired_state: Navigation, cards, tables, details and the graph's textual equivalent are usable from a narrow phone width upward, nothing overflows horizontally, and the core content is in the HTML.
non_scope: Hiding content below a breakpoint instead of adapting it
Requiring JavaScript to discover a documentation link
facts.risk: Mobile behaviour is the requirement most often declared done from a resized desktop window. It is asserted at real viewport widths by a browser check.

nodes.label: I1017
nodes.summary: Live state is an overlay that degrades to nothing

acceptance_criteria: Live updates use the process's existing event transport rather than a new one
Live values are visually and structurally distinguishable from snapshot values
The static projection renders the useful equivalent — what the endpoint is, and that the value is available when a server runs — rather than an empty card
Reconnection is bounded and backs off, and a failed connection does not produce a request storm
facts.current_state: The process has a health capability and peers. No surface subscribes to anything.
facts.desired_state: Live values arrive over the existing transport, are visibly distinct from the snapshot, and are absent rather than stale where no backend answers.
non_scope: A transport invented for the Cockpit alongside one that already exists
A reconnect loop with no bound
facts.risk: Live overlays are where credentials leak into browsers. Everything sent to the client is an allowlisted safe field.
facts.why: Live state is what makes a control plane worth opening. It is also what makes a static page lie, so it has to be an overlay that is visibly absent rather than a field that is silently stale.

nodes.label: I1018
nodes.summary: The surface rules exist as checks, proved by making them fail

acceptance_criteria: A change to an authoritative source that leaves any derived surface stale fails the drift check, and the failure names the source to change
A public or developer-facing capability that is not discoverable through the generated interface fails, unless it declares itself internal
A capability with behaviour carries verification appropriate to its kind, decided by typed policy rather than by one rule for everything
A developer-facing capability resolves to canonical documentation, and the coverage is visible rather than only reported
The static and runtime representations must remain equal after runtime-only fields are removed, enforced by the parity test
Each rule has a negative test that proves the check fires, and CI executes every one
facts.current_state: Project rules exist with checks for derived files, projections, hot paths, benchmark coverage and scope. None concerns UI exposure, capability documentation or verification policy.
facts.desired_state: Each rule has a check, each check has a negative test that proves it fires, and CI runs all of them.
non_scope: A rule with no executable check
Requiring documentation or a test from purely descriptive metadata
Duplicating a constraint an existing rule already enforces
facts.risk: Five new rules can make ordinary contribution feel like litigation. Each policy is typed by capability kind so that a descriptive object is not asked for a behavioural test.
facts.why: Everything in this milestone decays the moment a change can land without a check noticing. A rule that exists only as a document is a suggestion wearing a uniform.

nodes.label: I1019
nodes.summary: One skill runs the whole loop, and is itself in the graph

acceptance_criteria: The skill sequences the existing commands rather than reimplementing their behaviour
It follows the existing skill contract and needs no special-casing to be registered
It appears in the graph, the interface and the search through the ordinary derivation
It is tested behaviourally, on a repository state where something is genuinely missing
facts.current_state: Skills are a registered kind with a contract. None covers this loop.
facts.desired_state: One skill does the whole loop, follows the existing skill contract, and appears in the graph, the interface and the search like everything else.
non_scope: Several thin skills where one is enough
A skill that reimplements what the commands already do rather than sequencing them
facts.risk: A skill that wraps commands adds a layer that can drift from them. It sequences and reports; it does not decide anything the commands do not.
facts.why: The loop this milestone creates should be runnable by a worker without knowing which command does which part. And a repository that models skills as data should have its own automation as one of them.

nodes.label: I1020
nodes.summary: The graph's health is answered by the doctor that already answers everything else

acceptance_criteria: The checks cover graph validity, identity uniqueness, relation resolution, projection freshness, required documentation and verification presence, and the absence of unsafe metadata
Every number reported is computed, not stated
The output is machine-readable and human-readable in the existing shapes
Each check delegates to the engine that already decides it
facts.current_state: The health capability aggregates index diagnostics, benchmark coverage and projection staleness.
facts.desired_state: The graph's verdicts join them, computed rather than asserted, in the same machine-readable and human-readable output.
non_scope: A separate diagnostic script or command for the Cockpit
A check that recomputes a verdict another engine already produces
facts.risk: Building the whole graph inside a blocking check makes the pre-commit hook slow enough to be bypassed, which the performance doctrine already refuses. Its cost is measured against that budget.

nodes.label: I1021
nodes.summary: A browser proves the interface, at the widths people use

acceptance_criteria: Desktop and mobile navigation, search and filtering, the detail view and graph initialisation are all exercised
Representative viewports from a narrow phone to a wide desktop are asserted, including the absence of horizontal overflow
The runtime-only surfaces appear when a backend is present and are not offered when it is not
Internal links resolve and the console is free of errors
Selectors are stable identifiers rather than presentational classes
facts.current_state: A probe script drives the Cockpit's routes and interactions in a real browser.
facts.desired_state: The probe covers the derived surfaces at representative viewports, uses stable selectors and runs in CI.
non_scope: Pixel comparison of a rendered graph
Selectors coupled to presentational class names
facts.risk: Browser tests are the flakiest thing in any suite. Bounded waits on stable selectors, and no sleeps.
facts.why: Everything in this milestone is finally judged by whether a person can open it. Server-side tests cannot see an overflowing table, a menu that does not open or a script that throws on load.

nodes.label: I1022
nodes.summary: Drift in any derived surface fails the build

acceptance_criteria: Every new artifact is part of the canonical target set and its check
A drift failure names the authoritative source to change, not only the generated file that differs
Generation is deterministic, so an unchanged repository never reports drift
CI executes the check on every change
facts.current_state: The generation check covers the existing target set.
facts.desired_state: The new artifacts are in the same set, and a drift failure names the source to change rather than the file that differs.
non_scope: A separate drift script for the new artifacts
facts.risk: A non-deterministic generator turns this check into noise within a day, and the response to noise is to disable the check.
facts.why: Generation without a check is a suggestion. This is the mechanism that makes every derived surface in this milestone actually derived.

nodes.label: I1023
nodes.summary: Nothing private reaches a published page

acceptance_criteria: Known credential variable names, credential-shaped values, raw authorization material and machine-absolute paths are all detected
A finding names the location and the kind and never the value
A negative test plants a synthetic marker and proves the check finds it
The check runs in CI on every change
facts.current_state: No such scan exists for the site or the Cockpit data.
facts.desired_state: One check inspects the generated data and the built site, reports findings by location and kind, and runs in CI.
non_scope: Printing any secret value while scanning
A general secret scanner competing with the repository's existing tooling
facts.objective: Scan the published graph, the static site and everything the client receives for credential material, private environment values and machine-absolute paths, and fail on a finding without printing it.
facts.risk: A scan tuned to be quiet finds nothing forever. The synthetic marker is what keeps it honest.
facts.why: This milestone publishes a description of everything the repository knows. That is exactly the artifact in which an accidental token or a developer's home directory would travel furthest.

nodes.label: I1024
nodes.summary: The interface has a weight, and it is measured

acceptance_criteria: The generated data size, the served HTML size, the initial script and style weight and the graph initialisation are all measured
The baselines live where the benchmark infrastructure already keeps them, with the environment recorded
Thresholds catch a material regression and tolerate ordinary growth, and the policy states which is which
Heavy libraries are absent from pages that do not use them, proved by measurement rather than by intent
facts.current_state: The benchmark infrastructure records distributions per command against a committed baseline. Nothing measures a page or an asset.
facts.desired_state: The interface's weight and initialisation are baselines like the commands', with thresholds that catch a real regression and ignore a byte.
non_scope: A new benchmark system beside the one that exists
A threshold so tight that ordinary content growth fails the build
facts.objective: Measure the generated data, the served HTML, the initial scripts and styles and the graph's initialisation, and hold them to budgets through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has.
facts.risk: Asset budgets provoke arguments about kilobytes. The threshold is set where it detects a category change, not a content edit.
facts.why: A derived interface grows with the repository by construction. Without a measured budget it becomes slow gradually, which is the way that never gets noticed.

nodes.label: I1025
nodes.summary: The federated model and its two projections are an architecture decision

acceptance_criteria: The record follows the repository's ADR format and frontmatter exactly and relates to the decisions it extends
It states the federated composition, the dual projection, progressive enhancement, availability as metadata and the conditional exposure of runtime surfaces
The alternatives — one central manifest, a client-side application fetching the API, a separate site generator — are recorded with why they were not taken
The consequences state what a new subsystem must do to appear, and what it costs when it does not
facts.current_state: ADR 12 establishes the Cockpit as a projection of the registry. ADR 13 establishes that web surfaces are discovered from their producers. Neither covers the composed graph or the static projection.
facts.desired_state: One record states the decision, extends rather than restates the two it follows, and says what would have to change to revisit it.
non_scope: Restating ADR 12 or ADR 13
An ADR that documents the implementation instead of the decision
facts.objective: Record the decision to compose the authoritative registries into one typed graph and to render it as two projections, with the alternatives that were real and the consequences that follow.
facts.risk: Written last, it becomes a summary of the code. It is written when the choice between composing and centralising is still open.

nodes.label: I1026
nodes.summary: The architecture explains itself, from inside itself

facts.current_state: The Cockpit has a document. The composed graph, the relation model and the contributor workflow have none.
facts.desired_state: One architecture document, reachable from the places a reader starts, and an interface that states its own mode, sources and revision.
non_scope: Duplicating the ADR's reasoning in prose
Repeating full instructions in every directory document instead of composing them
facts.objective: Document the graph, its sources, its relation model, its two projections and the contributor workflow, and let the interface say how it was generated and from what.
facts.risk: A document explaining a derivation goes stale faster than the derivation. Every value it states about the current repository is generated rather than typed.

nodes.label: I1027
nodes.summary: A synthetic capability proves the architecture instead of describing it

acceptance_criteria: The capability is registered only at its authoritative source, and no surface is edited
After generation it appears in the graph, the interface, the search, the navigation and the static projection
Omitting its required documentation or verification fails enforcement with a message naming what is missing
Supplying the evidence makes every check pass
The fixture is removed afterwards, or kept only where test fixtures belong
facts.current_state: Nothing proves the loop end to end.
facts.desired_state: One test registers a synthetic capability, generates, and asserts its appearance everywhere it should appear — and asserts the failure when its required evidence is missing.
non_scope: Leaving the synthetic fixture in the repository as if it were a real capability
Special-casing the fixture anywhere in the implementation
facts.risk: A fixture that the implementation learns to recognise proves nothing. It has to be ordinary in every respect.
facts.why: Every claim in this milestone reduces to one: adding something requires no edit to any surface. That is either demonstrable or it is marketing, and the demonstration is cheap.

nodes.label: I1028
nodes.summary: The inventories this replaces are removed, not left running beside it

acceptance_criteria: The inventories that are replaced are enumerated from the repository, not assumed, and each is either removed or justified as authoritative for something else
Every consumer reads the derivation after the removal
Nothing that was removed is reachable as a fallback path
The built site and the running interface show the same content as before the removal, except where the derivation is more complete
facts.current_state: Several surfaces assemble their own lists. Which ones exactly is a reconnaissance result, not an assumption.
facts.desired_state: Each replaced inventory is deleted, its consumers read the derivation, and nothing hand-written survives as a fallback.
non_scope: Deleting a list that is genuinely authoritative for something the graph does not model
Leaving a hand-written list in place as a fallback
facts.risk: Removing a list that quietly held something the graph does not model loses content. Each removal is checked against what the derivation actually produces.
facts.why: Two systems doing the same job is worse than either alone: the old one keeps working just well enough that nobody notices it has diverged. Migration is finished when the thing it replaced is gone.

nodes.label: I1029
nodes.summary: The gate refuses what would silently break the interface

acceptance_criteria: A stale derived surface, a missing required document, a missing required verification, a broken static link to a runtime-only surface and unsafe published metadata each fail the gate
The browser checks and the parity test run on every pull request
Caching keeps the added time proportionate, and the total is measured
No check added here lives outside the existing verification hierarchy
facts.current_state: The verification workflow runs the repository's existing checks.
facts.desired_state: The new checks belong to the same gate, run on every pull request, and the gate stays fast enough to be usable.
non_scope: A separate workflow for the interface checks
A gate slow enough that people work around it
facts.risk: Browser checks in CI are where a suite becomes unreliable. They run against a built artifact with bounded waits, or they do not run at all.
facts.why: Every mechanism in this milestone depends on failing loudly at merge time. Without the gate they are conventions, and conventions are the thing this repository builds machinery to avoid needing.

nodes.label: I1030
nodes.summary: The milestone is accepted on its evidence

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of the milestone has evidence recorded against it
The coverage matrix baseline is recorded as a starting measurement rather than presented as a verdict
The contributor workflow runs exactly as documented on a clean checkout
Pre-existing failures, failures introduced here and failures fixed here are distinguished explicitly
Remaining limitations are stated rather than omitted
facts.current_state: Open.
facts.desired_state: Accepted with evidence against every criterion, with the coverage baseline and the limitations written where they will be found.
non_scope: Reporting a derived surface as proved without the artifact that proves it
facts.objective: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measurements are recorded with their environment, the contributor workflow runs as written, and the remaining gaps are stated.
facts.risk: The end of a large milestone is where intent gets recorded as outcome. Anything not demonstrated is written as a limitation.
facts.why: A milestone is accepted by its evidence. What a later reader has is the record, not this session.

nodes.label: start-here
nodes.summary: The documents that explain this repository are read in a fixed order

nodes.label: M000
nodes.summary: Milestone and DAG driven development

acceptance_criteria: The canonical model parses, rejects unknown keys, and refuses a duplicate id
A dependency cycle, a self-dependency and an unknown dependency are each rejected with a named finding
READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, VERIFY, DONE and CANCELLED are derived from recorded facts and stored nowhere
Execution waves are computed from the graph, and overlapping scope inside one wave is reported
The Mermaid DAG is generated from the same graph the CLI reads
GitHub milestones and issues are created and updated from the canonical model, and drift between them is reported
The website renders the roadmap, every milestone, every issue and the DAG from generated data
Every surface agrees: the CLI, the site data and the GitHub projection report the same issue set and the same READY set
Changing one dependency changes every surface
CI refuses a push whose canonical model is invalid or whose generated artifacts are stale
non_scope: A hosted planning backend or database
A second project-management vocabulary; milestones and issues are the only new nouns
Bidirectional GitHub write-back into the canonical files
Estimation, burndown, velocity or any scheduling model
risks: The engine is shell and awk; a graph large enough to make that slow would need a different implementation. Measured, not assumed.
GitHub is a projection. If a human edits a generated issue body, the next sync reports drift rather than silently overwriting it, which means drift can accumulate unattended.

nodes.label: M001
nodes.summary: A blocking question survives a handover

acceptance_criteria: A behavioural case demonstrates the current escape, so the gap is executable rather than asserted
The choice between transferring the question and widening the gate is recorded as a decision with what was rejected and why
The chosen behaviour is implemented and a case fails when it is removed
The claim in docs/CLAIMS.yaml moves to guaranteed with a real implementation path and a real test path
The claim detail page states what the behaviour does not cover
facts.desired_state: The behaviour is decided between two named alternatives, implemented, proved by a behavioural case, and the claim moves from planned to guaranteed with its implementation and test filled in.
non_scope: A question that blocks across repositories or worktrees
Assigning a question to a person, or notifying anybody
Any change to the finish contract's other lines
facts.outcome: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.

nodes.label: M002
nodes.summary: A durable record names the worker that wrote it

acceptance_criteria: A record written while another worker's task is active is attributed correctly or refused by name
The attribution can be checked from the record alone, with no conversation history
No new record type and no registry of workers is introduced
A behavioural case reproduces two workers writing in one checkout
facts.desired_state: Attribution is verifiable from the record alone. Where the tool cannot establish who wrote something, it says so and refuses rather than guessing from what happens to be active.
non_scope: A registry of named workers, personas or agents
Any identity the repository has to maintain, or that outlives the session that used it
Locking a checkout to one worker
facts.outcome: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.

nodes.label: M003
nodes.summary: A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical

acceptance_criteria: A session opens, closes, and its closed record is immutable, temporally ordered, and interpretable against current git through the existing divergence vocabulary
A closed session names the tasks, issues, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions of its episode by reference, and copies none of their bodies
Knowledge discovery is driven by git rather than by a filesystem walk, and an untracked file is not a source
A node identity survives a rebuild, and editing one source changes only the nodes derived from it
Every edge carries the file it was observed in; an edge without provenance is a validation failure
A second sync with no source change reports no work and is measurably cheaper than a cold one
Every read-only knowledge and session command leaves `git status` byte-identical
Shared and operational knowledge are separable, and a test proves the shared projection contains no operational record
`context` can carry a bounded knowledge section that is dropped before any immutable fact and is named under EXCLUDED when it is
Each new guarantee is a declared doctrine with a validator that doctor and watch dispatch, a claim, and a behavioural case
docs/CONTINUITY.md and docs/DESIGN.md state the new architecture precisely instead of contradicting it
non_scope: Any database, embedding, vector store, or similarity ranking
Any model invocation, network call, or generated summary
A second mutable narrative store that copies decisions, questions or checkpoint bodies
Publishing operational records to the website
Renderer-specific knowledge output for any particular note-taking application
Inferring a relationship from prose that does not state it explicitly

nodes.label: M004
nodes.summary: Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice

acceptance_criteria: Every public command in share/commands.yaml is a benchmark target without a second list anywhere
Cold and warm distributions are recorded separately with p50, p95 and p99 and never mixed
A local run is persisted under .ai/local/benchmarks/ and never treated as a baseline
The committed baseline is updated only by an explicit command on a clean tree
bench --check exits non-zero on a regression over the policy thresholds and names the command, the metric, both values and the threshold
Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command, proved by the work counters in a case
A cache hit and a cache miss produce byte-identical command output for every read-only command, proved by a case
doctor on this repository runs under the budget the policy declares, and the pre-commit hook inherits it
The performance rules are project rules under .ai/repo/rules/project, and docs/PERFORMANCE.md is the reference the README points at
non_scope: Any change to apps/majordomus-cli, whose measured latency is not the problem
A metrics database, a dashboard, a tracing backend or any telemetry service
Hot reload or filesystem watching
A persistent capability result cache across processes beyond the flatten cache
Benchmarking external services
risks: A cache is a second thing that can be believed. The flatten cache is keyed by the content hash of the file it caches, so a stale entry cannot be read for a changed file; it can only cost a miss.
Wall-clock thresholds are noisy across machines. The regression policy is conservative and relative, the structural counters are exact, and only the counters gate CI strictly.
Batching reads changes how validators are written. Each rewrite is proved by the case that already exists for the validator, run before and after, plus the counter case.

nodes.label: capability-graph
nodes.summary: One capability graph, two projections, and no second inventory of what this repository can do

acceptance_criteria: The graph composes the existing authoritative registries and introduces no second store of what they own
Every node has a stable identity that survives a title change, identities are unique, and generation is deterministic over identical inputs
Relations are typed, inferred only from stable conventions, and a relation that does not resolve fails generation with a message naming both ends
The static and the runtime projections come from the same graph, and their representations are equal once runtime-only fields are removed
A surface that requires a running backend is not offered as usable in the static projection, and that decision comes from availability metadata rather than from any check on the page's location
Navigation, overview, detail, search and the coverage matrix are all derived, and adding a capability requires no edit to any of them
The coverage matrix reports documentation, tests, enforcement and benchmarks only where an artifact or a resolved relation supports the claim
The Cockpit is usable on a narrow phone viewport and its core information is present before JavaScript runs
Each enforcement rule introduced here has a check that CI executes, proved by a negative test
non_scope: A hand-maintained menu, page list or capability inventory in any format, including a YAML one
Replacing any registry that is already authoritative for what it owns
A client-side application framework; the Cockpit stays server-rendered with progressive enhancement
A layout description language with coordinates, columns or component trees as data
An external search service for a graph this size
Mutating controls in the Cockpit beyond what the existing authorisation architecture already makes safe

nodes.label: cost-per-accepted-outcome
nodes.summary: Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data

acceptance_criteria: Cost is reported only for outcomes that were accepted by the finish contract
An outcome without telemetry reports no cost rather than a modelled one
The denominator is a real acceptance, never a count of sessions
facts.current_state: Not started, and not startable: it needs execution telemetry underneath it.
facts.desired_state: A completed, accepted task can state what it cost, from measurement rather than estimate.
non_scope: Any figure derived from elapsed time or token count as a proxy for progress
facts.outcome: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.
facts.problem: Cost per token is not a useful unit of work. The unit that matters is what an accepted outcome cost, and that cannot be computed without both telemetry and an acceptance record.
risks: Accepted outcomes are rare enough early on that the number is noisy; it must say so.

nodes.label: execution-telemetry
nodes.summary: Execution telemetry, only from providers that expose it honestly

acceptance_criteria: Telemetry is recorded only where the provider reports it
A provider that reports nothing produces an explicit absence, never a guess
The record is durable and readable back through the existing history surface
facts.current_state: Not started. docs/ECONOMICS.md states what it would take and deliberately claims nothing.
facts.desired_state: A completed task carries measured execution facts, or an explicit record that the provider did not supply them.
non_scope: Estimating a number a provider does not report
facts.outcome: Execution telemetry is recorded for providers that report it truthfully, and absence is recorded as absence rather than estimated.
facts.problem: Nothing here measures what a session actually consumed. Every economic statement about AI-assisted work in this repository is currently an argument rather than a measurement.
risks: A provider's self-reported usage may itself be unreliable; the record must say who reported it.

nodes.label: fly-deployment
nodes.summary: A deployment is a projection of the repository model, and a reachable URL is its evidence

non_scope: Any dependency, in code, script, documentation, CI or default, on ~/dev/prismatic-platform
A provider abstraction covering hosts other than the one this repository deploys to
Kubernetes, Nomad, buildpacks, Nixpacks or a second container implementation
A persistent volume, a database or any stateful service, unless a measured requirement forces one
Mutating deployment operations exposed to unauthenticated HTTP or to the browser
Profile-guided optimisation

nodes.label: foundation
nodes.summary: A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described

acceptance_criteria: One canonical policy projects to every provider and drift is detectable in one command
A task declares scope, and work outside it is reported
A finish contract is evaluated rather than asserted
Every enforced rule is declared in a registry, dispatched from it, and proven to reach its command
Every behaviour has a case in the suite and CI runs it
facts.desired_state: Unchanged: this milestone is the base every later one is measured against.
non_scope: Measuring tokens or cost
Constraining a provider's runtime
risks: The floor is bash 3.2 and BSD userland, which bounds what the engine can be asked to do.

nodes.label: routing-recommendations
nodes.summary: Routing recommendations derived from measured cost

acceptance_criteria: Every recommendation names the measurements it was derived from
Insufficient data produces no recommendation rather than a weak one
The recommendation is advisory and never silently changes a profile
facts.current_state: Not started, and gated on cost per accepted outcome existing at all.
facts.desired_state: A worker can ask which profile a class of task should use and get an answer traceable to measurements.
non_scope: Automatic routing without a person's decision
facts.outcome: The profile a task should run under is recommended from measured cost per accepted outcome, and the recommendation names the data it came from.
facts.problem: Choosing which capability to send a task to is currently a judgement nobody can check. A recommendation not derived from measured outcomes is an opinion with a command around it.
risks: A recommendation that is followed becomes a cause of the data that justifies it.

nodes.label: runtime-adapters
nodes.summary: Profiles become runtime constraints rather than advice

acceptance_criteria: At least one runtime limit is derived from the profile and applied, not merely printed
The limit is opt-in and a repository that does not want it is unaffected
A behavioural case proves the limit changes what happens, not only what is reported
facts.current_state: Not started. The profiles exist and project correctly; nothing derives a runtime limit from them.
facts.desired_state: Starting a task under a profile constrains what the worker may do, and the constraint is visible in the same place the profile is.
non_scope: Provider-specific behaviour that cannot be verified from this repository
facts.outcome: A profile's axes become opt-in runtime clamps a provider actually applies — read size, output condensation, subagent budget — with the limit derived from the profile rather than configured twice.
risks: Only providers that expose a real knob can be clamped honestly; the rest would be theatre.

nodes.label: shared-policy
nodes.summary: Shared policy across repositories and workers

acceptance_criteria: A shared policy can be consumed by more than one repository without copying it
A local override is explicit and survives an update of the shared source
Drift between the shared policy and a repository's effective policy is reported by one command
facts.current_state: Not started. Everything the tool does today is scoped to a single checkout.
facts.desired_state: One policy statement governs many repositories, and every deviation from it is visible rather than assumed.
non_scope: A hosted service, a registry, or any component that must be running for the tool to work
facts.outcome: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.
facts.problem: Policy is per repository. An organisation running many repositories has no way to state a rule once, and no way to see where it is not being followed.
risks: Shared policy is where a local tool becomes a distributed one; the offline guarantee has to survive it.

nodes.label: majordomus.project-integrity@1

nodes.label: majordomus.projection-integrity@1

nodes.label: majordomus.questions-store-integrity@1

nodes.label: majordomus.retention-caps@1

nodes.label: project.interfaces-are-projections@1
nodes.summary: External interfaces are projections of one capability definition

facts.statement: A capability is defined once and every external interface is derived from that definition; an interface that carries a definition of its own is a bug.

nodes.label: project.native-cli-documented@1
nodes.summary: A native command line command exists only with its documentation and its executable examples

nodes.label: project.never-author-identity@1
nodes.summary: Never author identity fields

facts.statement: repository_id, branch, head, working_tree and changed_files on any record are computed from git and never written by hand.

nodes.label: project.never-store-transcripts@1
nodes.summary: Never store or summarise transcripts

facts.statement: No record stores or summarises a conversation; records carry what is true now and the next action.

nodes.label: project.no-claim-without-test@1
nodes.summary: No claim without a test

facts.statement: A capability sentence in README.md or docs/ is backed by a case in test/cases/ or is phrased as a target.

nodes.label: project.no-counts-in-prose@1
nodes.summary: No counts in prose

facts.statement: Prose never states a number the repository can compute; it states the command that computes it.

nodes.label: project.no-network-no-eval@1
nodes.summary: No network, no telemetry, no eval, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion

facts.statement: bin/, lib/, share/ and test/ contain no network client, no telemetry, no eval, no curl piped to a shell, no silent overwrite and no recursive deletion outside a temporary directory.

nodes.label: project.no-new-nouns@1
nodes.summary: No new nouns

facts.statement: The tool gains no agents, personas, roles, tiers or registries beyond the vocabulary it has.

nodes.label: project.optional-complexity@1
nodes.summary: Complexity is optional, not ambient

facts.statement: Keep the core closed and the edges open; a change may add sophistication behind a stable mechanism, never mandatory complexity in front of the ordinary path.

nodes.label: project.performance-evidence@1
nodes.summary: A performance claim carries its measurement

facts.statement: No speed-up without numbers, no budget without a run behind it, no baseline update without a reviewable diff; observed values live in the benchmark history and the baseline file, never in prose.

nodes.label: project.portable-shell@1
nodes.summary: Portable shell

facts.statement: bash 3.2 and BSD userland are the floor: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no GNU-only flags, and shellcheck -x -s bash passes on every script.

nodes.label: project.rule-is-a-doctrine@1
nodes.summary: A new enforced rule is a doctrine, not an inline check

facts.statement: A rule the tool enforces is declared as a rule object with an x-majordomus block and a validator named mj_validate_<name>; no command selects checks by hand.

nodes.label: project.rust-benchmark-coverage@1
nodes.summary: No endpoint of the Rust executable without a benchmark, and no number without evidence

nodes.label: project.rust-canonical-declaration@1
nodes.summary: One canonical declaration; modules compose capabilities; the root composes modules

nodes.label: project.rust-cli-evidence@1
nodes.summary: The Rust executable carries its evidence with it

nodes.label: project.rust-command-tested-in-file@1
nodes.summary: A command asserts in the file that declares it that it is what it claims, and is composed rather than registered

nodes.label: project.rust-hot-path@1
nodes.summary: A request never rebuilds canonical state, and a cache is never trusted without an equivalence test

nodes.label: project.scope-is-declared@1
nodes.summary: What a worker reads is declared once, and nothing outside it is read or served

nodes.label: project.shared-server-resilience@1
nodes.summary: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out

nodes.label: project.tests-run-in-disposable-repos@1
nodes.summary: Tests run in disposable repositories

facts.statement: Behavioural cases run through bash test/run.sh in a temporary repository each, never against this checkout.

nodes.label: project.unknown-keys-are-errors@1
nodes.summary: Unknown configuration keys are errors

facts.statement: Every configuration file rejects a key nothing reads, and every state field is both written and read.

nodes.label: project.use-case-evidence@1
nodes.summary: A use case is proved by execution, and a capability is covered by a use case

nodes.label: project.web-surface-topology@1
nodes.summary: A web surface is discovered from its producer, never registered twice

nodes.label: deploy-site
nodes.summary: Deploy the site by hand

inputs: the commit to publish, checked out with a clean tree and contained in origin/master
zola, node_modules (npm ci) and, for the full gate, cargo
the operator's word, in this session, that the site is to go live now
outputs: a gh-pages commit naming the source commit, or a refusal naming the gate that stopped it
a checkpoint recording the deploy and the commit it published

nodes.label: implement
nodes.summary: Implement a change

inputs: the requested change, in the requester's words, with any issue or specification it names
a checkout with git history and the effective context for every path the change will touch
the repository's verification, generation and drift-check commands
outputs: the change, as coherent commits whose messages name what each proves
behavioural evidence that distinguishes the new behaviour from the old
regenerated projections and a clean drift check
an implementation record naming the invariant, the evidence, what was reconciled and what remains unsupported

nodes.label: repo-review
nodes.summary: Repository review

inputs: a checkout of the repository with git history available
the scope under review, or the whole repository when none is given
the effective context for every path in scope (majordomus context resolve <path>)
outputs: findings, each with severity, evidence, location, the smallest correct fix and the evidence that would prove it
the list of what was checked, including the areas where nothing was found

nodes.label: accept-or-refuse-finished-work

nodes.label: add-a-use-case-and-prove-it
nodes.summary: Add a use case and let the tool prove it

facts.summary: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

nodes.label: adopt-an-existing-repository
nodes.summary: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules

facts.summary: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

nodes.label: block-acceptance-on-an-open-question
nodes.summary: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered

facts.summary: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

nodes.label: capture-the-prompts-that-started-the-work
nodes.summary: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it

facts.summary: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: carry-a-blocker-across-a-handover
nodes.summary: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking

facts.summary: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

nodes.label: checkpoint-long-work
nodes.summary: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day

facts.summary: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

nodes.label: classify-what-belongs-in-the-context
nodes.summary: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data

facts.summary: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

nodes.label: complete-an-issue-only-with-its-evidence
nodes.summary: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists

facts.summary: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

nodes.label: deliver-issues-in-waves
nodes.summary: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one

facts.summary: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

nodes.label: document-every-directory-of-the-layer
nodes.summary: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing

nodes.label: extend-what-the-executable-serves
nodes.summary: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it

facts.summary: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

nodes.label: find-an-object-without-reading-everything
nodes.summary: Find an object of the layer without reading everything

facts.summary: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

nodes.label: find-out-what-drifted
nodes.summary: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked

facts.summary: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

nodes.label: follow-a-skill-the-repository-defines
nodes.summary: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one

facts.summary: Read the repository''s skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

nodes.label: gate-ci-on-the-tool-itself
nodes.summary: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract

facts.summary: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

nodes.label: hand-work-between-sessions
nodes.summary: Hand unfinished work to the next session

facts.summary: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

nodes.label: keep-decisions-out-of-the-transcript
nodes.summary: Record a decision so the next worker can find it

facts.summary: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

nodes.label: keep-the-bootstrap-thin-and-within-budget
nodes.summary: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget

facts.summary: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

nodes.label: know-which-tool-is-running
nodes.summary: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis

facts.summary: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

nodes.label: let-the-provider-draw-the-episode-boundary
nodes.summary: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to

nodes.label: migrate-from-the-old-layout
nodes.summary: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer

facts.summary: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

nodes.label: open-and-close-a-session
nodes.summary: Record what one worker did in one sitting

facts.summary: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

nodes.label: plan-the-work-as-data
nodes.summary: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate

facts.summary: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

nodes.label: prove-a-rule-is-enforced
nodes.summary: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down

facts.summary: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

nodes.label: prove-performance-with-benchmarks
nodes.summary: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression

facts.summary: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

nodes.label: read-back-what-happened
nodes.summary: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap

facts.summary: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

nodes.label: read-only-the-context-that-fits
nodes.summary: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped

facts.summary: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

nodes.label: read-the-rules-the-tool-applies
nodes.summary: See which rules apply here and what enforces them

facts.summary: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

nodes.label: record-a-decision-before-it-is-forgotten
nodes.summary: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you

facts.summary: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

nodes.label: resume-from-a-prompt-asset
nodes.summary: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript

facts.summary: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

nodes.label: resume-in-the-right-worktree
nodes.summary: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task

facts.summary: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

nodes.label: run-several-workers-at-once
nodes.summary: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding

facts.summary: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

nodes.label: see-what-the-repository-holds-without-reading-it
nodes.summary: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file

facts.summary: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

nodes.label: serve-the-layer-to-ai-clients
nodes.summary: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server

facts.summary: Open the repository in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

nodes.label: trace-a-change-to-the-context-it-affects
nodes.summary: Trace a change to the context documents it affects

facts.summary: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

nodes.label: trust-the-policy-before-reading-it
nodes.summary: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated

facts.summary: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.
